title: Adjust proration when retry-induced usage duplicates occur
creator: Ari Patel
description:
Summary:
When Stripe webhook retries or exporter retries occur during transient failures, some usage events are being recorded more than once in our billing export pipeline. Duplicate usage combined with our current proration and invoice-line merging logic can produce incorrect proration amounts on mid-cycle invoices and cause NetSuite export reconciliation failures.

Observed behavior (pattern):
- A quota/rate-limit burst causes a request to be rate-limited and retried at the API tier. The API emits duplicate usage events (same customer, same window, different internal event_id) to the aggregation layer.
- The hourly aggregator does attempt dedupe in a best-effort way but relies on ephemeral worker state; partial exporter failures (S3/DB timeouts) allow duplicates to persist across retry boundaries.
- Our proration step currently computes midcycle invoice amounts by summing invoice line candidates and then applying a post-merge rounding/proration pass. Duplicates inflate the summed units, pushing rounding logic into a different branch and producing small but cumulatively material proration deltas.
- Downstream NetSuite export merges invoice lines using a different bucketing/rounding heuristic, which causes mismatches and duplicate correction credits in accounting.

Root cause hypotheses: 
- Idempotency keys are not consistently propagated from ingestion -> rollup -> export. Some retry paths re-create events without the original idempotency token.
- The dedupe window is too short relative to potential exporter retry delays (current window 45s, observed retry propagation up to ~4m under client retries).
- Proration algorithm expects canonicalized per-customer interval buckets; duplicate events break the invariants and trigger fallback rounding branches.

Reproduction steps (dev/staging):
1) Deploy a synthetic replay script that submits a burst of usage events for a test account with controlled retries (client replays + server-side retry).
2) Force exporter write failure (S3 simulated timeout) to trigger retry logic.
3) Run hourly aggregator and export pipeline, capture intermediate aggregator output and final Stripe/NetSuite export CSV.
4) Compare invoice-level token counts and proration amounts to baseline (no retries).

Proposed fix (phased):
Phase 1 (safety + detection, 1 week):
- Ensure idempotency token is attached to canonical usage record and persisted in aggregation DB (schema change: add exported_idempotency_token as indexed varchar).
- Increase dedupe window to 8 minutes for high-retry customers, configurable by feature flag.
- Add an auditor metric and alert: "billing.export.duplicate_event_rate" that triggers >0.25% duplicates in a 1h window.

Phase 2 (corrective logic, 2 weeks):
- Make exporter writes idempotent at the export transaction level (persist export transaction row with idempotency token; skip double-write).
- Change proration math to perform per-source canonicalization before merge: compute proration on deduped canonical buckets, then apply NetSuite-compatible rounding (bankers rounding per-currency storefront rules).
- Add reconciliation runbook and a tool that: 1) identifies duplicate invoice-lines by matching customer+currency+period+external_key, 2) emits synthetic credit lines in a draft export for manual review.

Phase 3 (backfill + monitoring, 1 week):
- Backfill job: scan last 90 days for exporter duplicates and generate a reconciliation plan; run in dry-run for 48h then apply on a test subset of customers.
- Post-fix: run full Nightly reconciliation job and validate NetSuite import simulation for a week before enabling auto-apply.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests cover retry + exporter failure paths and assert idempotent export semantics.
- Staging replays (N=5) show zero duplicate exported usage records for the synthetic burst test within the configured dedupe window.
- NetSuite simulated import for repaired invoices has no mismatched totals for the 30-day test window.
- Alert firing threshold and dashboard added to console-ops; on-call runbook documented.

Rollout plan and risk mitigations:
- Feature-flag all behavioral changes; enable for 5 pilot customers on Dedicated region A for 72h, then expand to all staging tenants.
- Backfill script is non-destructive by default (creates correction export drafts instead of applying); require billing-team sign-off before applying credits.
- Keep existing export compatibility: new export rows include legacy_export_id for compatibility with current NetSuite mapping.

Testing & observability:
- Add end-to-end integration test that replays 10k events with randomized retry gaps and asserts dedupe rate <0.1%.
- Dashboard panels: duplicate_event_rate, exporter_write_retries, proration_delta_histogram, netsuite_reconciliation_mismatch_count.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.com/display/BILLING/Retry+duplicate+investigation (draft)
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7152 (exporter idempotency)
- Reconciliation job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-scripts/tree/main/reconciler
- Staging export sample: s3://redwood-staging-billing/replay-samples/dup-replay-2026-01-10.csv

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Deduping aggressively risks dropping legitimately distinct events with the same idempotency token if clients re-use tokens incorrectly. We should detect and surface suspicious client behavior separately.
- Increasing dedupe window raises memory/index pressure; need to evaluate DB index TTL and compaction.
- NetSuite rounding policy varies by currency; we must ensure our banker-rounding choice matches accounting expectations per currency.

Next steps (short):
- [Ari] finalize Confluence doc with observed export diffs and sample CSVs (2d)
- [Jordan] spike exporter idempotency implementation and schema change (3d)
